what_changed: Accuracy 0.06 -> 0.18 (output-marginal learning); per-unit CKA of mass class means at the block 0.36 -> 0.71; mass decodable at the value token kappa 0.53 (embedding identity), not causal anywhere (all IIA ~0.09). Group-gradient agreement: unit-1 mass examples conflict with unit 0 (attn2 +0.20, mlp_in +0.20, mlp_out +0.13) while unit 2 agrees with unit 0 (+0.46-0.49).
hypothesis: Unit 1 (scale 5) receives gradients that pull the shared weights in a different direction from units 0 and 2; if this conflict persists, unit 1 will form its own mass route at formation (as in the seed-700 precursor), i.e. gradient conflict precedes and predicts a representational split.
evidence: Observation: unit-1 gradient cosine with unit 0 is 0.13-0.28 vs 0.46-0.56 for unit 2, across all tensor groups. Correlation only; no representation exists yet. Speculation: the seed-700 split also involved unit 1 (different seed, different network). Head relocation events at this step are a matching artifact (near-uniform attention; heads indistinguishable), not real relocations.
key_question: Is the unit-1 gradient conflict a stable property of the task (unit 1 needs a different conversion) or transient noise of early training?
best_experiment: Track u0~u1 vs u0~u2 gradient agreement and per-unit CKA (pairwise) over steps 200-900; if conflict persists and per-unit CKA for unit 1 drops at formation, the hypothesis is supported.
intervention_rationale: Early phase: no causal representation (block IIA 0.09), nothing to organize; edits at this stage were rejected or ineffective in the precursor (doc 27).

what_changed: Accuracy 0.18 -> 0.24, block IIA 0.09 -> 0.14 (still not causal). Matched panel: equivalent pairs are closer at the block (cos 0.998) than different-mass pairs (0.949) or different-acceleration pairs (0.933). Group-gradient pattern flipped: unit 0 vs unit 2 now orthogonal (-0.03 to +0.01), unit 1 agrees weakly with both (+0.15 to +0.27). MLP: 102 neurons in the M*A (product) family, 47 answer-F family (none causally important yet).
hypothesis: (a) The step-100 unit-1 conflict was transient optimisation noise, not a stable property (refuted as a stable effect). (b) A unit-invariant (canonical) mass geometry exists in the block BEFORE the block is causally used: decodability-before-causality.
evidence: Observation: gradient cosines changed sign/ranking between 100 and 200 (transient). Observation: equivalent-pair block cosine 0.998 vs other-mass 0.949. Correlational only; block IIA 0.14, so the geometry is not yet used. Product-family neurons: eta^2 selectivity only (no ablation effect).
key_question: When the block becomes causal (IIA >= 0.5), does it keep this equivalence-preserving geometry (shared code across units) or does it split into unit routes as in the seed-700 network?
best_experiment: Track equivalent vs other-mass block distance on the matched panel, per-unit-pair CKA, and the interaction share through the formation window; compare with the moment IIA crosses 0.5.
intervention_rationale: Early phase; the only eligible targets are iia/ood_dev and there is no causal code to strengthen; the precursor showed early edits fail S2 and do not create codes faster than training.

what_changed: Loss plateau: accuracy 0.243 (+0.005), block IIA 0.15. Equivalent input pairs now receive the same prediction 0.90 of the time (0.52 at step 200), while block geometry keeps equivalents closer (cos 0.998) than other masses (0.940). Per-unit CKA 0.96. Gradient groups re-converged for units 0/2 (+0.25 to +0.38); unit 1 is again the outlier in attn2 (+0.01) and mlp_out (+0.00). attn2.h1 alone reduced the IIT loss this interval (-0.023).
hypothesis: The network's OUTPUT already respects mass equivalence (same answer for the same canonical mass) before mass is causally localised in the block; equivalence is computed somewhere other than the block at this stage (candidate: the MLP reading layer-1/attn2 features). Unit-1 gradient conflict recurs in attn2/mlp_out specifically (oscillating, not monotone).
evidence: Observation: equivalent-pair agreement 0.90 at 24% accuracy (the answer distribution is not constant: accuracy is above the 1/13 chance and OOD differs). Correlational: block equivalence geometry. Causal: none yet (block IIA 0.15, all heads ~0.07).
key_question: Where is equivalence computed during the plateau, if not causally in the block?
best_experiment: Interchange at dims 16-63 and at layer-1 tokens for M on OBS (patch tool) at the next checkpoint where IIA moves; if neither carries M causally, equivalence agreement is driven by coarse output statistics rather than a mass variable.
intervention_rationale: Early phase, plateau; no causal target to strengthen, and formation-window edits are better informed once the code appears.

what_changed: Block interaction share jumped 0.05 -> 0.36 while per-unit CKA rose to 0.996; acceleration became more separable at the block (other-acc cosine 0.928 -> 0.971, i.e. the block now IGNORES acceleration more). MLP: mass-family neurons appear (M 20, A 12) alongside m/a input families; the product family shrank 83 -> 40. attn2.h1 again the main IIT-loss reducer (-0.033).
hypothesis: (1) The interaction jump with near-perfect per-unit CKA means the units share the SHAPE of the mass configuration but at unit-specific offsets/rotations: a route split can begin invisibly to CKA. (2) The 0.88-0.90 equivalent-pair agreement is not evidence of a mass variable: it reflects coarse output statistics (zero-status), because nothing is causally used yet.
evidence: Causal (Level 2, OBS interchange): acceleration at its layer-1 tokens 0.059, output factor S at dims 16-63 0.064, mass at its layer-1 tokens 0.068, block 0.153 -> no variable is causally used anywhere (all near the chance-like floor). Observation: CKA is rotation/scale invariant by construction, interaction is not; both measured on OBS. Speculation: zero-status explanation of equivalence agreement (to be checked once accuracy rises above the zero-case share).
key_question: Is the rising interaction an early unit-specific rotation that will become the formation-time route split, or noise in a block that still carries little mass variance?
best_experiment: Watch interaction and pairwise per-unit CKA after normalising for mass-variance magnitude; the onset of causal IIA will show whether the split carries into the causal code.
intervention_rationale: Early phase and no causal variable exists (Level-2 tests); an interaction-removal edit now would act on noise and is not eligible (early-phase targets are iia/ood_dev only).

what_changed: Plateau continues (acc 0.254, IIA 0.159). Group-gradient conflict has disappeared: all mass-unit pairs agree +0.31 to +0.51 in every tensor group. Interaction share 0.36 -> 0.40; mass-unit identity consolidated in the block (mu@block). Pooled edit and copy both 0.10 (chance-like).
hypothesis: The lineage engine's head 'relocations' since step 100 are matching artifacts: layer-1 heads 1 and 3 have near-identical role-attention signatures, so the Hungarian assignment swaps them while still reporting 'confident' (cosine >= 0.8) matches. The registered confidence rule lacks a margin criterion.
evidence: Level 2 (feature records): B-he-0002 alternates attn1.h1 / attn1.h3 at steps 0-500 with match cosines 0.977-0.998, all labelled 'confident'; B-he-0006 alternates attn1.h1/h2/h3 (0.92-0.99). Same swaps in A. This is a property of the matcher, not of the network.
key_question: How much of the lineage-event stream is matching ambiguity rather than real change, and how should it be reported?
best_experiment: Post hoc (report, disclosed): for every head/cluster match compute the best-vs-second-best similarity margin from stored evidence; flag matches with margin < 0.05 as ambiguous and exclude their relocation events from claims. The registered matcher keeps running unchanged so records stay consistent.
intervention_rationale: Early phase; no causal code. The finding concerns the measuring instrument, not the network.

what_changed: Mass multiplicative (discrete-log) character at h rose 0.35 -> 0.47, the first sign of the circular calculator code; equivalent-pair block cosine dropped 0.996 -> 0.990 and different-mass 0.931 -> 0.918 (mass separation growing); interaction 0.40 -> 0.30. Accuracy flat 0.246, IIA 0.166. Gradient groups agree (+0.13 to +0.48).
hypothesis: Formation is approaching: in the seed-700 network the discrete-log circle formed 1-2 checkpoints before block IIA rose (doc 25). Prediction (falsifiable): block IIA(M) will exceed 0.3 within 300 steps and the multiplicative character will exceed 0.7 before or with it.
evidence: Observation: mult-char trajectory 0.60 (100) -> 0.45 -> 0.40 -> 0.39 -> 0.35 -> 0.47; precursor pattern from doc 25 (different seed, correlation only). No causal change yet (all IIA 0.07-0.17).
key_question: Will the circle form before causal use again (a reproducible ordering across seeds), and will the route split accompany it?
best_experiment: Keep the Level-1 audit; at the first checkpoint with block IIA >= 0.3 run the head anatomy inspection (which heads write mass, per-unit CKA per head) to compare with seed 700's head-0/head-2 story.
intervention_rationale: Early phase; prediction registered above so that the formation-window decision can be judged against it.

what_changed: Silent reorganisation: behaviour flat (acc 0.239, IIA 0.176) while weights moved fast (relative change per 100 steps: attn1.qkv 0.46, W_out 0.43, attn2.qkv 0.37, attn1.o 0.35, the largest so far); MLP neuron identities churned (stable 19 vs 94 at 600, relocated 36). Block now separates masses (other-mass cosine 0.918 -> 0.848) and accelerations (0.972 -> 0.902). Route@block and A@mlp consolidated. Mult-char at h fell back 0.47 -> 0.34.
hypothesis: The network is rebuilding its internal basis on the plateau (large, coordinated weight motion with no behavioural change) before formation; the loss landscape is flat here, so this phase is not an edge-of-stability phase.
evidence: Observation: weight-update magnitudes and neuron-identity churn. Level 2 (Hessian power iteration on the training objective): sharpness 15.1, Adam-preconditioned 10.4 vs edge 2/lr = 1,001 -> two orders of magnitude below the edge. My step-600 prediction (circle before causal use, IIA > 0.3 by 900) is weakened by the circle's fall but not yet falsified.
key_question: Is the reorganisation leading toward formation (a causal mass code) or is the plateau extending?
best_experiment: Next checkpoint: block IIA, copy and mult-char together; if IIA rises with weight motion slowing, formation has started.
intervention_rationale: Early phase (IIA 0.18); rapid basis rotation means any edit now targets a transient basis.

what_changed: Plateau extends: acc 0.243, IIA 0.158 (-0.018). Mult-char at h fell again 0.34 -> 0.27; interaction rebounded 0.23 -> 0.41; weight motion slowed (attn1 no longer in the top updates; W_out 0.25). Equivalent-pair prediction agreement fell to 0.54 (from 0.77).
hypothesis: The step-700 basis rotation did not initiate formation; seed 701 has a longer plateau than seed 700. My step-600 prediction (IIA > 0.3 by step 900, circle first) is now likely to fail; the circle's rise at 600 was a fluctuation, not a precursor.
evidence: Observation: three consecutive checkpoints of falling mult-char (0.47, 0.34, 0.27) with flat IIA. The equivalence-agreement drop (0.77 -> 0.54) together with flat accuracy supports the step-400 reading that this metric reflects coarse output statistics, not a mass variable.
key_question: What is the network learning during the plateau, if not mass? Candidate: the answer distribution conditioned on zero-status and the output unit.
best_experiment: At 900, check F decodability at the MLP and acceleration/product families against accuracy; a rise in F kappa without IIA would mean output-side learning precedes the mass variable.
intervention_rationale: Early phase. The only eligible targets would be iia/ood_dev; nothing indicates a code that a small edit could strengthen.

what_changed: Plateau persists (acc 0.249, IIA 0.159); my step-600 prediction (IIA > 0.3 by 900) is FALSIFIED. Mass decodability at the value token consolidated (kappa 0.50); answer F not decodable in the MLP (0.076). One MLP cluster split (B-ne-0046).
hypothesis: The plateau is a degenerate partial solution, not a wrong algorithm: the network detects zero answers and otherwise emits constants; it has not broken the symmetry needed to use mass or acceleration. It is not the doc-12 sign-ambiguity trap.
evidence: Level 2 (new read-only predictions tool, disclosed): predicts 0 for exactly the 17.7% of OBS questions whose answer is 0 (228/228), and otherwise mostly 8 (678) and 12 (241); agreement with F 0.249, with -F 0.228 (not a sign trap), with unit-ignoring variants 0.25 (chance-level after zeros); discrete-log agreement with F modulo 2/3/4/6 = 0.49/0.31/0.25/0.15 = chance -> no coarse multiplicative structure either.
key_question: Will the network escape the zero-plus-constant plateau on its own (as other mass_only seeds did), and does escape happen through the mass block or elsewhere?
best_experiment: Keep the predictions tool in the routine at each checkpoint until accuracy leaves 0.25; record which candidate function first rises above chance (F, a unit-ignoring variant, or the product without the output unit).
intervention_rationale: Nothing to reorganize: no mass, acceleration or calculation is used. Pushing the network off the plateau would be extra optimisation (the spec forbids crediting it to supervision); the precursor showed early edits fail behaviour-preservation. Decision: observe.

what_changed: Output distribution diversified (predictions now spread over 0, 5, 12, 3, 7 instead of mostly 8): accuracy 0.267 (+0.017). Equivalence geometry in the block is eroding: equivalent-pair cosine 0.975 -> 0.943 (different masses 0.840). Mass decodable in the block rising slowly (kappa 0.19 -> 0.22); attn2.qkv and attn2.o now among the largest updates.
hypothesis: The network has started to move off the zero-plus-constant solution by spreading its nonzero answers, but not yet by using mass: the block's early shared (unit-invariant) geometry is being dissolved before a causal code exists, i.e. symmetry breaking happens first in the readout/answer distribution.
evidence: Observation: prediction histogram changed; all candidate-function agreements stay within ~0.02 of the zero-plus-chance baseline (F 0.267, acc-unit-ignored 0.268, log mod 4 0.264 vs 0.25) -> no specific function yet. Causal: block IIA 0.167, layer-1 0.096, heads 0.07 (none used).
key_question: Which candidate function will rise above baseline first, and does the shared block geometry need to dissolve before the causal mass code can form?
best_experiment: Continue predictions + matched-panel tracking; when any agreement exceeds the 0.25 baseline by >= 0.05, run the head anatomy to locate the first causal writer.
intervention_rationale: Still early phase with no causal code; the change is in the answer distribution, which an edit would only perturb.

what_changed: Formation began: mass multiplicative character at h jumped 0.31 -> 0.81 (discrete-log circle formed in one interval); accuracy 0.27 -> 0.31; F decodable in the MLP 0.10 -> 0.17; three MLP clusters became causally supported (partial) by ablation for the first time; the block geometry reorganised wholesale (equivalent-pair cosine 0.94 -> 0.71, different masses 0.84 -> 0.63); large weight motion (W_out 0.67, W_in 0.43, attn2.qkv 0.35).
hypothesis: (1) The mass unit conversion is learned before the acceleration conversion (mass is the declared variable). (2) Unit 1 (scale 5) is converted differently at the layer-1 value token in this seed as in seed 700, so the unit-1 route split is a property of the task's arithmetic, not of one seed. (3) No head is yet the dominant mass writer; one will be selected in the next few hundred steps.
evidence: Level 2 predictions: agreement with 'acceleration unit ignored' 0.316 = F 0.311 > 'mass unit ignored' 0.274 (causal-behavioural, supports 1). Level 2 head anatomy: value-token per-unit CKA 01 0.84 vs 02 0.92 (correlational, supports 2, cross-seed with doc 25/27); heads 0, 1, 3 each attend ~0.3 to the mass value; head 0 writes the most mass variance (interaction 0.34; CKA 0.09-0.30 across units), head 1 shares units 0/2 (0.77) but not unit 1 (0.34). Block IIA still 0.16 -> the circle is not yet used through the block.
key_question: Which head will become the dominant mass writer, and will it inherit the unit-1 split from the value token?
best_experiment: Next checkpoint: head anatomy again plus block IIA; a head whose mass variance grows fastest and whose attention to the mass value exceeds 0.6 is the writer; compare its per-unit CKA with the value token's.
intervention_rationale: Still early phase (VAL IIA < 0.5). No defect is established: in seed 700 the unit-1 route was the organisation that persisted, and removing it later cost generalisation (docs 25, 27). An edit now would also hit a writer that has not yet been selected.

what_changed: Rapid formation: accuracy 0.31 -> 0.61, OOD_DEV 0.16 -> 0.31, block IIA 0.16 -> 0.48, copy 0.18 -> 0.50, pooled inversion edit 0.10 -> 0.35, mult-char 0.81 -> 0.95, M kappa at the value token 0.62 -> 0.84, M-family MLP neurons 26 -> 98, F decodable in the MLP 0.39. Different-mass block cosine fell 0.63 -> 0.39 while equivalents rose 0.71 -> 0.84 (a canonical mass axis is forming in the block). Neuron identities churned (10 stable).
hypothesis: (1) Head 0 has been selected as the dominant mass writer (as in seed 700) with head 3 as a secondary writer. (2) My step-1,100 claim that the unit-1 split is a cross-seed property is REFUTED at the writer level: head 0's code separates unit 2 (CKA 0-1 0.74, 0-2 0.44, 1-2 0.11). (3) This network forms a much more editable mass code than seed 700 (0.35 vs 0.04-0.07 at the same stage); prediction: editability will FALL as the interaction (0.29 now; head-0 0.54, head-3 0.60) consolidates, as happened in seed 700 (0.45 -> 0.66).
evidence: Level 2 head anatomy (causal-adjacent): head 0 attends 0.52 to the mass value, mass between-class variance 28.8 (head 3 9.6, heads 1-2 <= 1.7); head-0 single-head IIA 0.14 (only head above floor). Value-token per-unit CKA became uniform (0.72-0.76). Causal: block IIA 0.48, copy 0.50; pooled persistent edit 0.35 (OBS). Prediction (3) is testable at the next checkpoints.
key_question: Does the editable code at formation survive consolidation, or does the interaction between mass and unit route grow and erase editability (the seed-700 trajectory)?
best_experiment: Track pooled edit, interaction (block and per head) and head-0 per-unit CKA over 1,300-1,600. If editability falls while interaction rises, the window to act is now-to-1,400, and a dry run of an interaction-limiting, route-preserving edit (with the stability lookahead) is the experiment.
intervention_rationale: VAL phase is still early (IIA < 0.5) so only iia/ood_dev targets are eligible, and there is no evidence yet that the current organisation is defective (editability is high). Wait one checkpoint to see whether prediction (3) holds before acting.

what_changed: Consolidation: accuracy 0.61 -> 0.82, OOD_DEV 0.31 -> 0.42, block IIA 0.48 -> 0.68, copy 0.78, pooled edit 0.35 -> 0.58, interaction 0.29 -> 0.36. Head 0 (46.5) and head 3 (25.8) write mass; each is strongly route-split (interaction 0.67 / 0.77) but the block total is only 0.36. 158 MLP neurons now match stably (identities settling).
hypothesis: (1) My step-1,200 prediction that editability would fall as the interaction grows is REFUTED here: both rose together, because the two writers' unit-specific parts partly cancel in the block. (2) The generalisation gap (ID 0.82 vs OOD_DEV 0.42) is caused mainly UPSTREAM: the layer-1 value-plus-unit binding behaves like a lookup of seen combinations, not a compositional value-rotated-by-unit-scale operation, so held-out combinations produce wrong canonical mass.
evidence: Level 2 (new read-only ood_locus tool, disclosed): canonical-mass probe at the value token 0.86 on ID vs 0.41 on OOD_DEV (block 0.62 vs 0.33); setting the block to the TRUE mass's FIT class mean raises OOD_DEV accuracy 0.42 -> 0.66 (label-using diagnostic: shows the downstream would mostly cope if mass were formed correctly); held-out mass combinations are worse (0.33) than held-out acceleration combinations (0.52).
key_question: Can the layer-1 binding be made compositional (value code rotated by unit scale) so held-out combinations form correct mass, without losing what the network already does?
best_experiment: Layer-1 compositional binding supervision: interchange the value token's and the unit token's layer-1 residuals separately with matched counterfactual targets (raw value from source with base unit; unit from source with base value), on FIT only, restricted to attn1 and the value embeddings. NOT available as a registered primitive (counterfactual supervision is defined only at the block, dims 16-63 and attn2 heads); recorded as a proposed primitive for a future registration.
intervention_rationale: The diagnosed defect lies at layer-1 token positions, which no registered primitive can target; block-level primitives act downstream of the failure (the label diagnostic shows the downstream is not the main bottleneck). Editability is high and rising, so there is no editability defect to repair either. Per the spec, a new primitive is proposed for future work rather than altering the frozen rules.

what_changed: accuracy 0.82 -> 0.92, OOD_DEV 0.42 -> 0.57 (the gap narrows 0.40 -> 0.35), block IIA 0.68 -> 0.82, pooled persistent inversion edit 0.58 -> 0.77, copy 0.93, interaction 0.36 -> 0.39; first fully causally supported neuron cluster (B-ne-0085); MLP identities settled (219 stable, 3 relocated). Equivalent inputs now get the same answer 0.94 at 0.92 accuracy.
hypothesis: Seed 701 is forming a canonical-like, highly editable mass organisation (PR #21's seed-600 regime) rather than seed 700's route-dependent one; the deciding factor is that the two writer heads' unit-specific parts cancel in the block (block interaction 0.39 vs 0.67-0.77 per head). Prediction: pooled edit stays >= 0.7 to the end without intervention.
evidence: Causal (OBS): block IIA 0.82, copy 0.93, pooled persistent edit 0.77 (seed 700 at maturity: about 0.12). Correlational: equivalent-pair block cosine 0.945 vs different-mass 0.213. The step-400 caution about the equivalence metric no longer applies, since accuracy is high.
key_question: Is there any organisational defect worth repairing, or only the generalisation gap, which is upstream and outside the registered primitives' reach?
best_experiment: Keep monitoring pooled edit, interaction and the OOD gap; if the gap stops narrowing while ID saturates, re-run ood_locus to see whether the upstream share of the failure changes.
intervention_rationale: No defect in organisation or editability; the remaining weakness (held-out combinations) was diagnosed at layer-1 binding (step 1,300), which no registered primitive targets. A gratuitous edit risks the post-edit instability documented in doc 27.

what_changed: Mature: accuracy 0.995, OOD_DEV 0.68, block IIA 0.90 (mass in the block now causally verified), pooled persistent edit 0.89, copy 0.99; interaction flat 0.385; MLP identities stable (226); weight motion slowing (largest update 0.13).
hypothesis: The remaining mass x route interaction in the block is not noise: it carries information the network uses for held-out unit-value combinations, as in seed 700. Prediction written in the dry-run proposal: interaction removable with OOD_DEV within +-0.01; falsifier: OOD_DEV falls by more than 0.01.
evidence: Level 2 causal dry run on OBS (installs nothing; p1500_interaction_dryrun.json; 2% of model norm; attention + MLP; KL, IIT, off-manifold KL and route-probe guards): interaction -0.222, editability +0.038, IIA +0.004, keep 0.998, route information +0.287, OOD_DEV -0.017 -> FALSIFIER MET. Cross-seed: the doc-27 precursor (seed 700) showed the same OOD cost for post-formation interaction removal.
key_question: What information does the residual interaction carry that helps held-out combinations, given that the held-out failure is mostly upstream (step 1,300)?
best_experiment: Compare, for held-out vs ID examples, the per-unit block offsets (route-specific cell means) the network produces; if held-out mass is placed near the correct unit-specific cell rather than the pooled mean, the interaction encodes unit-specific placement that partly compensates for wrong fusion.
intervention_rationale: The only candidate with a real organisational effect fails the generalisation check (S3) on OBS; editability is already 0.89, so there is no editability defect to repair. A dry run answered the question without risking the trajectory.

what_changed: Small regression in everything at once: accuracy 0.995 -> 0.964, OOD_DEV 0.68 -> 0.64, IIA 0.90 -> 0.88, pooled edit 0.89 -> 0.82, copy 0.99 -> 0.96; mass in the block fell back to partial causal support (M@block weakening). Largest update moved to attn1.qkv.bias (0.13). Interaction 0.39 -> 0.36. Neuron identities still stable (237).
hypothesis: An ordinary training loss spike (edge-of-stability style, learning rate ~1.9e-3), not reorganisation: everything degrades together and identities stay stable. Prediction: recovery to >= 0.99 accuracy within 200 steps. Because A = B here, this is a baseline for how often unedited training spikes in this window, which matters for attributing post-edit collapses (doc 27).
evidence: Observation: simultaneous small drops in all metrics with neuron identities stable (237) suggest a uniform disturbance; the attn1 bias update is unusual for a settled network. No causal test needed beyond the routine audit. (Not done: the step-1,500 'unit-specific placement' experiment, deferred until the network is stable again.)
key_question: Does the network return to the same organisation after the spike (attractor, as in doc 27), and does editability recover fully?
best_experiment: Compare pooled edit, interaction and head anatomy at 1,700-1,800 against 1,500.
intervention_rationale: Editing during a spike would compound instability (doc 27) and confound attribution.

what_changed: Full recovery from the 1,600 spike and beyond the 1,500 level: accuracy 0.999, OOD_DEV 0.72 (best so far), IIA 0.93, pooled edit 0.94, copy 0.998; interaction 0.36 (unchanged organisation); M-family neurons 99 -> 130; M@block back to fully causally supported. Weight motion small (max 0.07).
hypothesis: (1) Step-1,600 prediction CONFIRMED: recovery within 100 steps to the same organisation (attractor). (2) The residual interaction is how the network places held-out masses: it produces correct answers for many held-out combinations whose canonical mass is NOT linearly decodable, i.e. via the unit-specific (non-linear) geometry.
evidence: Level 2 ood_locus: block given the true mass's class mean -> OOD_DEV 0.94 (downstream almost perfect; actual 0.72) so the gap is upstream; held-out-mass-only 0.61 vs held-out-acceleration-only 0.85; linear M probe on OOD_DEV at the value token 0.41 and block 0.33 while the network gets 0.72 right -> correct held-out answers are produced without a linearly readable canonical mass. Together with the step-1,500 dry run (removing the interaction cost 0.017 OOD_DEV) this supports (2); still correlational for the mechanism.
key_question: Can held-out mass formation be improved without removing the unit-specific geometry that partly compensates?
best_experiment: Requires the layer-1 compositional-binding primitive proposed at 1,300 (not registered). Within the registered primitives, test whether off-manifold KL alone (noise_kl) with a small route-preserving translation improves OOD_DEV on OBS, as a dry run, at the next quiet checkpoint.
intervention_rationale: Network just recovered from a spike; I wait for a quiet checkpoint before any dry run, and no installed edit is justified by evidence yet.

what_changed: Quiet: accuracy 0.997, OOD_DEV 0.726, IIA 0.93, pooled edit 0.94 -> 0.90, copy 0.998, interaction 0.355; weight updates <= 0.06; neuron identities 249 stable; two new partially causal neuron clusters (B-ne-0089/0090).
hypothesis: No combination of the REGISTERED objective terms acting upstream can improve held-out formation, because none of them encodes compositional value-unit binding; such edits can raise editability but will cost generalisation.
evidence: Level 2 causal dry run on OBS (p1800_ood_upstream_dryrun.json; attn1+attn2 only; KL, IIT, noise KL, translation, route probe; 2% of model norm): OOD_DEV -0.026 (prediction confirmed), editability +0.036, interaction -0.098, unit-transfer -0.159, keep 1.000, route information +0.33. Together with the 1,500 dry run: two different registered recipes both trade generalisation for organisation in this network.
key_question: Is there any remaining organisational property worth improving whose improvement would not cost generalisation?
best_experiment: None available within the frozen primitives; the decisive experiment (layer-1 compositional binding supervision) is recorded for a future registration. Continue observation; re-check the OOD locus at 2,500 and 4,000.
intervention_rationale: The editability gain on offer (+0.04 on an already 0.90-editable network) would cost 0.026 held-out accuracy, a trade-off the spec says is not a success. The evidence-based decision is not to edit.
previous_interventions: none (two dry runs, both showing a generalisation cost)

what_changed: ID perfect (1.000) but OOD_DEV fell 0.726 -> 0.663; large UPSTREAM weight motion in a mature network (attn2.qkv 0.24, attn1.o 0.23, attn2.qkv.bias 0.16, attn1.qkv 0.16), neuron identities less stable (209 stable, 28 uncertain); IIA 0.93 -> 0.91, pooled edit 0.90 -> 0.87.
hypothesis: ID-silent upstream drift: once the training task is solved, training keeps reshaping the layer-1 binding and the mass writers in directions that are invisible on familiar questions but change held-out formation. Held-out accuracy is therefore not settled after convergence, and its checkpoint-to-checkpoint variance must be considered when comparing the two networks at 6,000.
